name: Bloom Filter
description: A Bloom filter is a space-efficient probabilistic data structure that tests whether an element is a member of a set. False positives are possible, but false negatives are impossible. It uses multiple hash functions to set bits in a bit array.
how_it_works: A Bloom filter uses a bit array of m bits and k hash functions. When adding an element, all k hash functions are applied and the corresponding bits are set to 1. When querying, all k positions are checked; if any bit is 0, the element is definitely not in the set. If all bits are 1, the element is probably in the set.

complexity.time: O(k) for both insertion and lookup, where k is number of hash functions
complexity.space: O(m) bits where m is array size, independent of element count

key_parameters: optimal_k: m/n * ln(2) minimizes false positive rate
pseudocode_or_diagram_description: Initialize m-bit array to 0. Insert(x): for i in 1..k: array[hash_i(x) % m] = 1. Query(x): for i in 1..k: if array[hash_i(x) % m] == 0: return 'definitely not in set'. Return 'probably in set'. Cannot delete without counting Bloom filter variant.
